ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, points $D$ and $E$ are the midpoints of sides $BC$ and $AB$ of the equilateral triangle $\triangle ABC$, respectively, with $AD=6$. If $F$ is a moving point on $AD$, what is the minimum value of $BF+EF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect CE, intersecting AD at F, and connect BF, then BF+EF is the minimum (according to the fact that the shortest distance between two points is a straight line; the perpendicular distance from a point to a line is the shortest),\\
$\because$E is the midpoint of AB, $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore CE\perp AB$\\
Since C and B are symmetric about AD, then BF+EF=CF,\\
$\because$In the equilateral $\triangle ABC$, BD=CD,\\
$\therefore$AD$\perp$BC,\\
$\therefore$AD is the perpendicular bisector of BC (three lines in one),\\
$\therefore$C and B are symmetric about the line AD,\\
$\therefore$CF=BF,\\
That is, BF+EF=CF+EF=CE,\\
$\because$AD$\perp$BC, CE$\perp$AB,\\
$\therefore$$\angle$ADB=$\angle$CEB=$90^\circ$,\\
In $\triangle ADB$ and $\triangle CEB$,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle ADB=\angle CEB\\
\angle ABD=\angle CBE\\
AB=CB
\end{array}\right.$ ,\\
$\therefore$$\triangle ADB\cong \triangle CEB$ (AAS),\\
$\therefore$CE=AD=6,\\
That is, BF+EF=\boxed{6}.

Since $E$ is the midpoint of $AB$ and $\triangle ABC$ is equilateral, $CE\perp AB$. Since $BD=CD$ in equilateral $\triangle ABC$, $AD\perp BC$, so $AD$ is the perpendicular bisector of $BC$. Also, $\angle ADB=\angle CEB=90^\circ$, and in $\triangle ADB$ and $\triangle CEB$, we have $\angle ADB=\angle CEB$, $\angle ABD=\angle CBE$, and $AB=CB$, so $\triangle ADB\cong\triangle CEB$ (AAS). Therefore $CE=AD=6$, so the minimum value is $\boxed{6}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows triangle ABC with A at the top, B at the lower left, and C at the lower right. Point D is on BC, and segment AD is drawn from A down to D. Point E is on AB. Point F lies on AD, with segments BF and EF drawn, matching the quantity BF + EF. From the given condition, D and E are the midpoints of BC and AB, and AD = 6. Reasoning: Since ABC is equilateral and D is the midpoint of BC, AD is the median and altitude to BC, so AD is the perpendicular bisector of BC. Therefore B and C are symmetric about line AD. For any point F on AD, reflection symmetry gives BF = CF. Thus BF + EF = CF + EF. By the triangle inequality, CF + EF is at least CE, with equality exactly when C, F, and E are collinear, i.e. when F is the intersection of CE with AD. So the minimum possible value of BF + EF is CE. Now E is the midpoint of AB, so CE is the median/altitude from C to AB in the same equilateral triangle. All such altitudes in an equilateral triangle have equal length, hence CE = AD = 6. Therefore the minimum value is 6.
